core_obligations: Prove additivity in the module argument from the two projections and right exactness (proof lines 1298-1305).
Define the second B-module structure and verify distributivity via the addition map N + N -> N (proof lines 1307-1314).
Prove that the canonical map N tensor_B F(B) -> TF(B, N) is B-linear for the second structure (proof lines 1315-1334).
Identify TF(B, B) tensor_B N with TF(B, N) for finitely presented N (proof lines 1315-1334).
proof_roadmap: Item (2): the second module structure (proof lines 1307-1314).
Items (3) and (4): linearity and the tensor identification (proof lines 1315-1334).
difficulty_reason: If for every B-algebra the functor TF(B, -) sends short exact sequences of B-modules to right exact sequences, the lemma derives four consequences: additivity in the module argument, the existence of a second functorial B-module structure on TF(B, N), B-linearity of the canonical map N tensor_B F(B) -> TF(B, N) with respect to that second structure, and an identification TF(B, B) tensor_B N = TF(B, N) for finitely presented N (statement lines 1270-1291). The proof is displayed item by item, each with its own argument: (1) from the two projections and the right exactness sequence, (2) by checking distributivity through the map N -> N + N -> N, and then (3) and (4) are reduced to the finitely presented case via the second structure (proof lines 1294-1334). The level is H3: four derived properties, with the second module structure -- the non-obvious device that makes the later items meaningful -- constructed and verified inside the card.
